1. Announcements - Faculty Senate President Williams

i. Today’s reception is being sponsored by the College of Pharmacy - Thank you Dean LaPlante!
ii. Call for Nominations: At the October Faculty Senate meeting, Sens. Kendall Moore, William Krieger, and Alison Roberts were chosen as this year’s Nominating Committee. Per Section 5.2 of the Senate By-Laws, the Nominating Committee shall prepare a slate of candidates for one (1) one-year and two (2) two-year vacancies on the Executive Committee. The Executive Committee Election shall be held May 7, 2026. Please reach out to a member of the Nominating Committee if you are interested in this role.

VP Preisser encouraged faculty to spread the word, and suggested that they explore relevant housing webpages or reach out to him directly for more information.

iv. ‘All-hands’ curriculum meeting prior to the start of fall semester 2026 - VP Preisser announced that the Faculty Senate and Vice Provost Adams are co-hosting a mandatory meeting on September 1, at 1 pm, aimed at improving curriculum proposal quality and review process consistency in Kuali. The meeting would be required for Deans and Associate Deans who have approval roles in the CMS and it is strongly recommended that the faculty chairs of college-level curriculum committees also attend. More information will be forthcoming but affected parties need to make sure this meeting is in their calendars.
2. Disposition of the Minutes - Faculty Senate President Williams
i. Minutes of the Faculty Senate Meeting of 3/12/26 were approved.

i. Executive Committee Meetings of March 6, March 13, and March 27, 2026 meetings. (No meeting on 3/20 due to Spring Break.)
d. Recommendations of the Faculty Senate Executive Committee: FSEC recommends the following bills:

i. Approval of Faculty Senate Meeting Calendar for AY 2026-2027. Pres. Williams noted that FSEC has recommended a meeting calendar that prioritizes ‘third Thursdays’ for consistency, while avoiding holidays, breaks, and cultural or religious celebrations that preclude work. The calendar was approved.
ii. Bill 2025-2026-FSEC-09: Amendments to UM 5.78.10 - 5.78.12 regarding the Joint Committee on Online and Distance Learning - Continued from the 2/19/26 And 3/12/26 meetings. Pres. Williams noted the proposal had been discussed by the faculty senate at previous meetings and is now offered for approval. It was moved to the senate docket for action by FSEC and was seconded. Questions were raised from the floor about some particulars of the bill and FSEC members responded. iii. Ratification of appointment to the Space Allocation Committee: Leon Thiem, representing the College of Engineering. A motion to ratify was approved.

iv. FSEC Bill 2025-2026-12 regarding precluding use of the Veteran’s Day holiday as an instructional day - VP Preisser noted that while State and Federal calendars list Veteran’s Day as a holiday, language in the University Manual does not preclude its use as an instructional day. FSEC sought to clear up any confusion via the proposed amendment, which was moved for action by FSEC and seconded from the floor. College of Education senators inquired whether or not the current proposal was the result of their petition last month to amend the University Manual to preclude the use of Indigenous People’sDay/Columbus (IP/C) Day as an instructional day. VP Preisser answered affirmatively, explaining that the detailed review of UM Sec. 8.70.25 that occurred with their proposal marked the first time the ACC, CBUM and FSEC had all taken an in-depth look at the relevant language in quite some time, and the question of Veteran’s Day seemed to warrant clarification independent of what happens with the IP/C Day legislation, which is still under consideration. In response to further questions, VP Preisser confirmed that approval of the subject bill does not preclude approval of the IP/C Day bill, but he acknowledged that the constrained number of available instructional days in certain fall semesters certainly makes the Calendar Committee’s work more challenging.

1. Bill 2025-2026-Joint-01, a joint proposal of the University Administration, FSEC, and the SCLC regarding reorganization of the Office of the University Ombuds. Also, the plan to professionalize the Office of the Ombuds had been discussed at previous senate meetings, including, most recently, the March 12 meeting. With no further questions or discussion, there was a motion and second to approve the proposal. The motion was approved.

Specialist Spitale explained that a pause in new Kuali submissions is planned for the summer months to allow system administrators the opportunity to make much-needed updates to workflows and user experience features. All proposals entered by 5/15 will still advance through the approval process to the Dean-level of review. Any proposal not approved by the relevant dean by 6/1 will revert to draft form. Such drafts will remain in the system and will still be viewable, but will need to be resubmitted at a later date to advance toward approval. Normal proposal submission procedures and workflows will resume on 8/15. Additional information is available via the Curriculum Toolkit on the Faculty Senate’s webpage. Questions from the floor were offered, including inquiries about the degree to which suggestions from the various college curriculum committees factor into the update. It was noted that the current effort is focused more on compliance with the curricular streamlining initiative approved by the faculty senate earlier this year, but it is hoped that this year’s initiative will lay the groundwork for future short pauses wherein incremental process improvements like those that would be suggested by the curriculum committees might be made.

ii. Bill No. 2025-2026-07B, Programs, covering multiple program modifications, including to specializations and minors, in the Colleges of Arts and Sciences, Business, Engineering, Health Sciences, and the College of the Environment and Life Sciences.

ii. Bill 2025-2026-06B, Programs, including several program modifications, along with new certificates and specializations.
c. Centers and Institutes Review Committee - Chair Porto - The CIRC is required to present annually on any new Centers and Institutes and on the rechartering status of other C/I’s reviewed. Tabled to the May 7 meeting.

d. Teaching, Advising, and Admissions Committee Annual Report- Chair Romanow praised her fellow committee members and noted they have had a very busy and productive year. The TAAC was involved in the review and approval of several key pieces of legislation this year, including the creation of a President’s List and modernizing the Second Grade Option. They were also involved in the curricular streamlining initiative and the reconfiguration of the Honors Program. As a result of legislation approved last year, the Committee now has a role to play in Admissions and is still determining, with AVP Libutti’s help, how that new charge will be implemented. In terms of future priorities, the Committee has been tasked with looking at UM provisions related to academic dishonesty, especially where it intersects with grade disputes. The Committee hopes to craft relevant amendments for consideration next year.

e.
Budget and Administration Committee Annual Report - Chair Triki explained that his committee’s primary task this year has been to try to measure faculty sentiment toward the new budget mode via a survey distributed broadly to the community.
As of now, the Committee intends, according to Chair Triki, to share their results with the Financial Strategy and Planning Office so that a conversation about improving messaging might be had.
It has not yet been decided how the data collected might otherwise be shared or disseminated.
Based on the survey results, the Committee had concluded that there seems to be a serious disconnect between the actual outcomes of the budget model roll-out and the faculty’s perception of those outcomes.
As examples, a majority of those surveyed did not see the new model as improving transparency or ensuring a more fair allocation of resources across colleges.
Chair Triki suggested that expanding dissemination of information about the details and mechanics of the budget might result in more positive perceptions.
VP Jenkins asked if current sentiment around higher education generally might have colored the survey results.

She enumerated several recent and ongoing concerns and challenges facing universities around the country (constrained research funding, various Federal actions, outside influence and interference in curricular matters, etc.) and suggested that the current landscape likely has a negative ‘baseline mood’ undercurrent that would be hard to measure.
Chair Triki agreed that the survey probably did roll out at an unfortunate time for measuring faculty understanding and satisfaction.
He noted that one positive takeaway from the results was the degree to which faculty are engaged and paying attention, and he praised their resilience in the face of unrelenting bad news.

f. Committee on Technology and Infrastructure Annual Report - Chair Wallace noted the many projects his committee tackled this year, including providing input to improve Brightspace and EdTech operations, helping to recreate a searchable classroom database, and suggesting strategies for improving the IT contracts/software approval process. Priorities for next year will include understanding faculty needs and habits around responsible AI use in research, and aiding in Brightspace file recovery and migration, among other things.

1 University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees Regulations Regarding Use of University Property [DRAFT 20241008 CC] Introduction As noted in the University of Rhode Island’s Mission Statement and consistent with University values, the University of Rhode (also “University” or “URI”) is committed to high- quality education, community engagement, and the freedom to learn, teach, create, and conduct research with integrity in the pursuit and dissemination of new knowledge aimed at contributing to the public good.
The management of University Property and other resources is paramount to meeting that mission.
Authority and Applicability Pursuant to Rhode Island General Laws §§ 16-32-2 and 16 -32-2.1, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees is empowered to make rules and regulations for the control and use of Univ ersity Property while the President of the University is responsible for the general management of University Property.

These regulations apply to all users of University Property , including all members of the University community (students, faculty, staff, and affiliates) and third parties (individuals, groups, and members of the public) who wish to use any University Property for any purpose.
Definitions University Operations.
All teaching , research, community engagement, and business functions, as well as any other official activity of the University.
University Property.
Property belonging to the State of Rhode Island and held in trust by the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees; property held by the University of Rhode Island or any of its component units in its own name; and property owned by third parties but assigned to, occupied by, or managed by the University or any of its component units.
University Property includes all real property, including without limitation land, buildings and other structures, fences, driveways and walkways, and other permanent improvements and associated infrastructure .
For the purposes of these regulations, property leased or licensed to a third party is excluded from the definition of University Property. 1.

General The primary purpose of University Property is to support the University’s mission.
Every individual and group using University Property is expected to use it in a manner that (i) complies with all applicable laws, policies, procedures, rules, and regulations; (ii) is safe and responsible; (iii) maintains and protects the integrity, cleanliness, and functionality of the University Property; (iv) does not materially and substantially disrupt or interfere with University Operations; and (v) does not impinge upon the individual rights of another person or group.

2 Access to and use of University Property is governed by the University, not by colleges, departments, or administrative units.
Individual colleges, departments, and administrative units may adopt guidelines governing the use of University Property allocated for their specific use provided that such guidelines are consistent with these regulations.
Space is allocated pursuant to the University’s policy on Allocation and Utilization of Space. 2.
Limitations and Prohibited Activities The University may establish reasonable standards and limitations regarding the time, place, and manner of use for any University Property, including access to certain areas within a building, entire buildings themselves, or specified areas of University Property, by both the general public and the University community.
The University also has the right to restrict access t o any and all University Property, including the campus(es) as a whole, as necessary to address safety and/or security concerns.

Specific requirements relative to the limitations and prohibited activities (e.g., building hours, decibel levels, posting, etc.) may be developed by the Department of Public Safety and posted on the Public Safety website. a.
Individual Rights : Under no circumstances may University Property be used in a manner that impinges upon the rights of another person under the United States or Rhode Island Constitution; any federal, state, or local law; or any University policy. b.
Violation of Law: Any use of University Property that violates federal, state, or local laws, regulations, or ordinances will constitute a violation of these regulations. c.
Disruption of University Operations : The use of University Property must not materially and substantially disr upt or interfere with the conduct of University Operations or scheduled meetings, programs, or events. d.
Campus and Building Access and Egress : Any use of University Property must not impede access to, use of, or egress from University Property (or otherwise impede access to or egress from sanctioned University functions and activities) or impede vehicular or pedestrian right-of-way.

Driving on walkways or accessing gated roadways unless authorized or otherwise posted is strictly prohibited. e.
Endangerment: The use of University Property may not be used in a manner that endangers others or is violent or incites violence. f.
Leafletting and Distribution of Literature : Leafletting or the distribution of literature is allowed provided that the activity does not impede the flow of pedestrian or vehicular traffic, block access or egress, or create litter; and the item is not placed on motor vehicles or forced upon others.
Housing and Residential Life and Dining Services may develop additional restrictions on leafletting specific to areas under their control. g.
Signs, Postings, Banners : Posting of information is limited to designated bulletin boards or other areas identified for pos ting.
Affixing signs unrelated to University Operations into or on University Property, other than designated areas, is prohibited.
Affixing signs or banners to the exterior of buildings without prior permission from the Offices of the Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs and Provost, Vice

3 President for Student Affairs , or Vice President for Administration and Finance is prohibited.
Except for within designated spaces dedicated to postings and announcements, printed matter such as posters, fliers, and stickers may not be affixed to University Property.
No signs supported by standards or st icks shall be permitted in any assembly inside any building on campus.
Signs supported by standards or sticks shall be permitted outside. h.
Graffiti: Graffiti is defined as u nauthorized and unlawful writings or drawings made on a wall or other surface.
Graffiti is not protected speech, and may be considered the illegal defacement of property, punishable as a crime under Rhode Island General Law (RIGL § 11-44-21.1).
Temporary markings, such as chalking, are permissible provided the speech is lawful and the markings are easily removable. i.
Erection of Structures : No structure, permanent or temporary, may be erected on University Property without the specific written approval of the Vice President for Administration and Finance.

Camping, defined as the erection of a temporary shelter or otherwise maintaining a space designed for living (eating, sleeping, etc.) outside, is prohibited without written permission from the Office of the Vice President for Administration and Finance or the Office of the Vice President for Student Affairs j.
Amplified Sound: Sound level must be maintained at a volume that does not interfere with University Operations; sound emission beyond the perimeters of the reserved area shall be at a reasonable level.
Specific requirements will be developed by the Department of Public Safety and posted to the Department of Public Safety website. k.
Building Access: Access to non-residential buildings shall not be permitted outside of posted hours unless specifically authorized by the responsible depart ment.
Access to residential buildings is by invitation only and the University reserves the right to ask guests to leave at any time. l.
Building Exteriors : Climbing, scaling, or rappelling on University Property is prohibited unless expressly permitted in writing by the Vice President for Administration and Finance or their delegate. m.
Bicycles, Skateboards and S imilar Conveyances.

The use of bicycles, scooters, skateboards, and similar means of motorized and non- motorized conveyance on University property ( except for mobility aids) may be controlled by specific requirements established by the Department of Public Safety. n.
Open Flames and Fire Safety : Any activity that includes the possession or use of fireworks or the use of fire pits, campfires, or torches without prior written permission by the University (and/or local or state fire authorities) are prohibited.
Protected candles (candles with wind screens) may be used with prior approval from the Department of Publ ic Safety.
The unauthorized or improper activation, possession, use, removal, or disabling of fire safety equipment and/or warning devices; failure to follow standard fire safety procedures; and/or interference with firefighting equipment or personnel are prohibited. o.
Sanitation: Urination or defecation in any place other than a designated restroom is prohibited.

4 3.
Enforcement and Violations Violations of this policy may lead to disciplinary actions up to and including termination from employment, suspension or expulsion from the University, revocation of affiliate status, or a permanent restriction or trespass from University Property.
Such discipline for students will be imposed under the Student Handbook and for employees under applicable Human Resourc e Administration policies, collective bargaining agreements, or other controlling agreements.
In addition, the Board of Trustees may impose fines, with a schedule determined by the Department of Public Safety, up to statutory limits plus associated costs pursuant to RIGL § 16-32-2.
Violations of these regulations may lead to removal from University Property, possible loss of further access to and use of University Property, and/or prosecution for trespass, disorderly conduct, or other offenses under state law.
The Department of Public Safety, along with any offices sponsoring or directly associated with an event, is responsible for enforcing any infractions of these regulations .

The Department of Public Safety may require adjustments, up to and including ce ssation, to the activities associated with any particular use of University Property should those activities violate the terms o f these regulations (or any federal, state, or local laws or regulations).
Users of University Property are responsible for any damage, loss, or destruction of University Property (including moveable property or the contents of a building) and may be assessed a fee for any cost incurred by the University as a result of any user’s violation of these regulations. 4.
Exceptions Except as otherwise set out in these regulations, exceptions to the limitations and prohibited activities delineated with in th ese regulations m ay only be granted through a written agreement with the University as may be entered into regarding a specific scheduled event pursuant to established processes of the University.
